subject: Orbit instrumentation compatibility checklist + rollout plan
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@orbit.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@orbit.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Orbit POC — instrumentation compatibility info

Hi Rachel / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking Orbit through a quick demo last week. We kicked off an internal POC to evaluate Redwood as our recommended inference runtime for customers that run Orbit alongside LangChain/LlamaIndex flows. The big ask from our engineers is: can Redwood ingest our lightweight ``orbit-trace`` hooks without major SDK churn?

Quick summary of what we need to validate in POC:
- Ability to attach a per-request trace id and get it propagated through the Redwood runtime (both hosted and Dedicated).
- Compatibility with LangChain agent wrappers and LlamaIndex retrievers without breaking streaming.
- Minimal changes to our JS/TS SDK (we prefer a shim layer vs full fork).

I've attached a rough SDK diff we iterated on (orbit-sdk-diff.patch) and a one-page list of the signals we want to collect. Can you confirm whether the Redwood SDK sidecar approach or an instrumentation shim will be faster to ship for a limited canary?

Proposed timeline:
- Compatibility checklist review: this week
- Instrumentation POC: 2 weeks
- Canary with 2 pilot customers: early Jan

If you can point us to a short checklist or a preferred integration approach, we can scope our engineering time.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Integrations, Orbit.ai
attachments: orbit-sdk-diff.patch (text/patch), orbit-integration-notes.pdf (summary)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@orbit.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@orbit.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Orbit POC — instrumentation compatibility info

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the patch. We can definitely move fast on this.

Short answer: we recommend starting with a lightweight instrumentation shim that talks to Redwood's trace headers and a small LangChain/LlamaIndex integration shim. That avoids forking your SDK and gives us a path to add automatic propagation later.

Action plan (short):
- I attached a working checklist (instrumentation-checklist.xlsx) that maps your signals to the Redwood header names and a minimal acceptance criteria column.
- Marissa will own the runtime compatibility tests (LangChain chaining + streaming). Jonas will own the canary routing + Dedicated config.
- We can provision a Dedicated POC pool for Orbit for 2 weeks; cost/commit details in the SOW draft.

Can you confirm: the shim runs in-process in your SDK (JS/TS) or as a small sidecar? Patch looked in-process but we want to verify memory/latency tradeoffs.

Next steps:
1) Samir to confirm shim model preference and pick two pilot scenarios (retrieval + agent).
2) Redwood to run the checklist and share results by Thu.
3) If green, we circulate a short SOW and get signatures for a Jan canary.

Looping in Marissa / Jonas for technical comments.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samir Shah <samir@orbit.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@orbit.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Orbit POC — instrumentation compatibility info

Thanks Rachel — quick technical notes from our runtime team after a first pass against the patch. (Quoted below for context.)

On Mon, 30 Nov 2026 at 17:03, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the patch. We can definitely move fast on this.
> 
> Short answer: we recommend starting with a lightweight instrumentation shim that talks to Redwood's trace headers and a small LangChain/LlamaIndex integration shim.

Marissa's notes (high-level):
- The orbit-sdk-diff.patch looks like it wires in a per-request header X-Orbit-Trace. Redwood runtime already preserves custom headers through routing; we just need to validate prefixing for KV-cache keys to avoid collisions. Test: run a 1k request stream with trace ids and confirm KV TTL invariants.
- LangChain: the common entry points are the AgentExecutor and the LLMChain. We can provide a small helper: Redwood-propagateTrace() that wraps send/stream calls. That should be 6–8 LOC in JS.
- LlamaIndex: retriever pipelines that call into embeddings + index lookups will need the trace id forwarded. We recommend adding the trace header into Redwood's streaming envelope rather than modifying LlamaIndex internals.
- Performance: baseline latency penalty for adding a single header is negligible; the risk is in adding synchronous disk writes for debug traces. Avoid blocking I/O in the shim.

I'll run the checklist tests and post results by Thu EOD. Jonas — can you scope the Dedicated pool ramp and the canary routing policy? We want an automatic fallback to hosted if the rimless pool hits X% error.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Integrations Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Orbit POC — instrumentation compatibility info

Great — this looks like the right approach and aligns with our engineers' preference for a shim. Quick answers:
- We'll implement the shim in-process (JS/TS) but keep the debug trace write async to avoid blocking.
- Pilot scenarios: (1) LangChain Agent with streaming responses; (2) LlamaIndex retriever + embedding cold-start.

We're happy to run the 1k request stream test once you provision the Dedicated pool. Please go ahead with the checklist tests; if you get green we can sign the short SOW and schedule the canary.

Linking our legal/procurement for the SOW — I've uploaded a short draft to the Drive and left comments in the PDF (orbit-poc-sow-draft.pdf). We'll expect a short DocuSign route for signatures.

Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Integrations, Orbit.ai
